newsitem.title: USA: Texas tornadoes damage seen at $25-50 million.
newsitem.headline: Texas tornadoes damage seen at $25-50 million.

text.p: A string of tornadoes that hit central Texas on Tuesday caused up to $50 million of damage, insurance experts said.
Elton Bomer, chairman of the State Insurance Commission, said on Wednesday morning that preliminary estimates put the total damage across the affected area at between $25 million and $50 million.
"That's a pretty rough estimate. We'll know more later in the week," Bomer said in the small town of Jarrell, which was hardest hit by the storms.
The most violent of Tuesday's tornadoes killed at least 27 people and destroyed about 50 homes in Jarrell. Bomer said damage to the town alone amounted to between $10 million and $20 million.
At least six twisters tore through four counties on Tuesday, wrecking an estimated 200 buildings. Torrential rain, heavy winds and baseball-sized hail caused further damage.

"The damage is much more widespread than we had anticipated," said Sharon Cooper, a spokeswoman with Allstate Insurance Company, adding that it was too soon to put a firm figure on the overall damage.
She said her insurance firm had received claims from 22 zip codes in Austin alone
A clutch of tornadoes which hit north Texas on April 10, 1979, including one that devastated Wichita Falls, killed 53 people and caused over $500 million in damages.
